prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Heeeey reddit wtf is that and why isn't alcohol working?

This was my very first syngonium. I absolutely will. Not. Lose. It. It started my love for syngoniums and i just cannot lose it. I have sprayed this thing down so many times in the last few weeks. I've used peroxide, alcohol, insecticide, neem, I tried fungicide as a last ditch! What is is and how to I make them disappear!?

I've had a nasty mealy problem for the last year ish but haven't lost a plant yet. These didn't look like mealies to I wasn't too sure what to do and everything either reeks and isn't working or smells slightly better and still isn't working.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: juvenile mealybugs (crawlers).** Young mealybugs are tiny, flat and only lightly fuzzy, so they don't look like the cottony adults you're used to. After a year of mealies in your collection, scattered white specks along the veins on the undersides fit that best.

**Why nothing is "working":** sprays only kill what they soak. Eggs sit inside waxy sacs, and bugs hide in the papery sheaths at the base of the stems (visible in your first photo), in leaf joints and in the soil. Each new hatch replaces what you killed. Fungicide and peroxide won't help, since this isn't a fungus. Repeated harsh sprays are probably why some leaves look dull and faded.

**Other possibilities:**
- **Shed skins from aphids or thrips.** Rub a few specks with a cotton swab. Mealybugs smear wet, sometimes pinkish. Skins flake off dry like dandruff, and live insects (green or black aphids, slim yellow or black thrips) will be somewhere nearby.
- **Whitefly nymphs.** These are flat, translucent ovals stuck tight to the leaf. Shake the plant: tiny white flies will flutter up.

**Fix:**
1. **Isolate and clean.** Rinse the plant hard in the shower, especially leaf undersides. Then swab every speck with 70% alcohol, peeling back or removing the stem sheaths. Cut off the worst leaves.
2. **Check the roots.** Unpot it and look for white cottony patches on the roots or pot wall (root mealybugs). If you find any, wash the roots, repot in fresh soil and scrub the pot.
3. **Treat on a schedule.** Use one product, like insecticidal soap or neem, every 5–7 days for 6 weeks so you catch each hatch. Better still, add a systemic such as imidacloprid granules in the soil, where legal.
4. **Treat your whole collection the same way**, or the bugs will keep coming back.
